newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rubber imports plunge as output rises.
newsitem.headline: Indian rubber imports plunge as output rises.

text.p: India's rubber imports fell 71 percent in the first five months of 1996/97 (April-March) as domestic production surged, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Sunday.
Imports of natural rubber between April and August fell to 8,950 tonnes from 31,280 tonnes in the same period last year, the news agency said.
Production of natural rubber during April-August totalled 196,000 tonnes, up from 174,000 in the same five-month period in 1995.
The country produced 21,408 tonnes of synthetic rubber, up from 21,063 tonnes in the same period last year, it said.
PTI said India's rubber board had asked the government to halt imports of natural rubber after studying the supply-demand situation.
India was expected to have a supply of 650,000 tonnes of rubber in 1996/97, with an opening stock of 103,000 tonnes and estimated production of 547,000 tonnes, the news agency said.
Demand for rubber was estimated at 578,000 tonnes in the current year, PTI said.
While production of natural rubber increased 12.6 percent in the first five months of 1996/97, consumption rose 11 percent to 234,000 tonnes, it said.
